# `vec`

Vectors of 2, 3 and 4 components of `f32` and `i32`, written in Colibri on top of the operator interfaces.

```colibri
import vec
```

Back to the [standard library index](README.md).

## Types

### `vec2`

```text
struct vec2 {
    x: f32
    y: f32
}
```

A float vector of 2 components, `f32` each; 4 bytes per component, laid out like C.

Implements `Add`, `Sub`, `Mul`, `Div`, `Mul[float]`, `Div[float]`, `Neg`, `Show`.

#### `vec2.dot`

```text
fn dot(self, other: vec2) -> f32
```

The sum of the products of the components, left to right.

#### `vec2.len_sq`

```text
fn len_sq(self) -> f32
```

The squared length.

#### `vec2.len`

```text
fn len(self) -> f32
```

The length, the square root of `len_sq`.

#### `vec2.distance`

```text
fn distance(self, other: vec2) -> f32
```

The distance between two points.

#### `vec2.normalize`

```text
fn normalize(self) -> vec2
```

The vector with the same direction and length 1; the zero vector stays zero.

#### `vec2.lerp`

```text
fn lerp(self, other: vec2, t: float) -> vec2
```

`self + (other - self) * t`

#### `vec2.to_ivec`

```text
fn to_ivec(self) -> ivec2
```

Each component truncated toward zero; a `nan` or a value out of range panics.

#### `vec2.abs`

```text
fn abs(self) -> vec2
```

#### `vec2.min`

```text
fn min(self, other: vec2) -> vec2
```

The smaller of each pair of components.

#### `vec2.max`

```text
fn max(self, other: vec2) -> vec2
```

The larger of each pair of components.

### `ivec2`

```text
struct ivec2 {
    x: i32
    y: i32
}
```

A integer vector of 2 components, `i32` each; 4 bytes per component, laid out like C.

Implements `Add`, `Sub`, `Mul`, `Div`, `Mul[i32]`, `Div[i32]`, `Neg`, `Show`.

#### `ivec2.dot`


The sum of the products of the components, left to right.

```text

```

The squared length.

#### `ivec2.len`

```text

```

The length, computed in `float` (never traps for a valid vector) and rounded once to `f32`.

#### `ivec2.distance`


The distance between two points, computed in `float` and rounded once to `f32`.

#### `ivec2.abs`

```text

```

Each component made positive; `i32` `MIN` panics.

## Functions

### `vec2`

```text
fn vec2(x: float, y: float) -> vec2
```

`vec2(x, y, ..)`: an untyped literal, an `f32` or a `float` is accepted, rounded to `f32`.

### `ivec2`

```text
fn ivec2(x: i32, y: i32) -> ivec2
```

`ivec2(x, y, ..)`

### `vec3`

```text
fn vec3(x: float, y: float, z: float) -> vec3
```

`vec3(x, y, ..)`: an untyped literal, an `f32` or a `float` is accepted, rounded to `f32`.

### `ivec3`

```text
fn ivec3(x: i32, y: i32, z: i32) -> ivec3
```

`ivec3(x, y, ..)`

### `vec4`

```text
fn vec4(x: float, y: float, z: float, w: float) -> vec4
```

`vec4(x, y, ..)`: an untyped literal, an `f32` or a `float` is accepted, rounded to `f32`.

### `ivec4`

```text
fn ivec4(x: i32, y: i32, z: i32, w: i32) -> ivec4
```

`ivec4(x, y, ..)`

### `from_angle`

```text
fn from_angle(radians: f32) -> vec2
```

The unit vector that points `radians` counter-clockwise from the x axis.

### `angle`

```text
fn angle(v: vec2) -> f32
```

The angle of a vector from the x axis, in radians, in `-PI..=PI` (`0` for the zero vector).

## Implementations for other types

These are written in this module for types it does not declare, so that, for example, a number can be the left side of an operator.

```text
impl Mul[vec2, vec2] for float {
    fn mul(self, v: vec2) -> vec2
}
```

```text
impl Mul[ivec2, ivec2] for i32 {
    fn mul(self, v: ivec2) -> ivec2
}
```

```text
impl Mul[vec3, vec3] for float {
    fn mul(self, v: vec3) -> vec3
}
```

```text
impl Mul[ivec3, ivec3] for i32 {
    fn mul(self, v: ivec3) -> ivec3
}
```

```text
impl Mul[vec4, vec4] for float {
    fn mul(self, v: vec4) -> vec4
}
```

```text
impl Mul[ivec4, ivec4] for i32 {
    fn mul(self, v: ivec4) -> ivec4
}
```
